semin-durr:2-2.t: His saying: {حتى زُرْتُمُ}: «حتى» marks the limit (ghāya) for His saying «أَلْهاكم», and it is conjoined to it.

semin-durr:4-4.t: His saying: {ثُمَّ كَلاَّ سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ}: Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn ibn Mālik treated it as verbal emphasis (tawkīd lafẓī) with a conjunction placed in between. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The repetition is an emphasis of the rebuke and the rejection of them, and «ثم» indicates that the second warning is more forceful and severe than the first, as you say to the one you advise: 'I tell you, then I tell you: do not do it.'" End of quotation. It is reported from ʿAlī, may Allah honour his face: "«كلاَّ سوف تعلمون» in this world, then «كلاًّ سوف تعلمون» in the Hereafter." On this it is not a repetition, since the two differ because the things they relate to differ. And «ثُمَّ» is in its proper sense of an interval of time. The object of knowing is omitted in the three verbs, because the aim is the act and not what it relates to. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The meaning is: if you knew the error in what you are doing, when you witness what you will return to." So he implied one object for it, as if he had made it mean "to know" (ʿarafa).

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ}: its apodosis (jawāb) is omitted, that is: "you would have done what cannot be described". It was also said that the implied form is: "you would have turned back from your disbelief". «عِلْمَ اليقين» is a maṣdar (verbal noun). It was said that its original form is al-ʿilm al-yaqīn (definite), so the described was annexed to its attribute. It was also said that there is no need for that, because knowledge can be certain or not certain, so it was annexed to it as the general is annexed to the particular. This shows that certainty (yaqīn) is the more specific.
Ibn ʿAbbās read «أأَلْهاكم», as an interrogative of affirmation and denial. In this it is reported: lengthening with easing (tasḥīl) of the hamza, and it is also reported with the full pronunciation of both hamzas without lengthening.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {لَتَرَوُنَّ}: this is the answer to an implied oath. Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Kisāʾī read «لتُرَوْنَّ» in the passive. It is transferred from the triliteral «raʾā» to «arā», thereby acquiring another object, so the first object stands in the place of the agent and the second remains accusative. The others read it in the active, taking it as not transferred, so it governs only one object, the seeing being by sight (baṣariyya). The Commander of the Believers, ʿĀṣim and Ibn Kathīr, in a report from them, read with fatḥa in the first and ḍamma in the second, meaning «لَتُرَوُنَّها»; and Mujāhid, Ibn Abī ʿAbla and al-Ashhab read with ḍamma in both. The majority hold that the two wāws are not hamzated, because their vowel is accidental; Makkī and Abū l-Baqāʾ stated explicitly that it is not allowed, and gave as the reason the accidental nature of the vowel.
Al-Ḥasan and Abū ʿAmr, with a disagreement reported from them, read with hamza on the two wāws, finding the ḍamma on the wāw heavy. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is disliked", meaning because the vowel is accidental on it. Yet they have hamzated what has more right to be left unhamzated than this wāw, for example {اشتروا الضلالة} [al-Baqara: 16], where some hamzated the wāw of «اشتَروْا», though its vowel is accidental and disappears in pause. The vowel of this wāw, though accidental, does not disappear in pause, so it has more right to be hamzated.

semin-durr:7-7.t: His saying: {عَيْنَ اليقين}: an emphatic maṣdar (maṣdar muʾakkid), as if it had been said "seeing with the eye", to deny the supposition of figurative sense in the first seeing. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "Because «raʾā» and «ʿāyana» have the same meaning."
